title: BeatStage 3D
observed_goal: The menu screenshots show the stated goal “hit the arrows on beat and outperform the group.” This goal was not observed during active gameplay or in a result. The official card also claims fast arrow chains and competition with three rivals, but this claim was not play-tested.
observed_controls: On the menu page, the arrows ← ↑ ↓ → are introduced as inputs; their acceptance during active gameplay was not observed.
On the menu page, Space for beat and Esc for pause are introduced; their functionality during active gameplay was not observed.
The metadata tested Enter, Space, ArrowUp, w, ArrowRight, and holding ArrowRight+Space for 900 milliseconds, but a frame change alone does not prove that the input was accepted.
observed_core_loop: Game loop not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive; the frames progress from loading and textual instructions to the main menu and show no clear sequence of input, feedback, repetition, and active-game result.
progress_feedback: The loading frames show 9%, 58%, and 85%; this is loading progress only, not score or game progress. Score, combo, timing, Fever, or rank feedback was not observed in the frames; the available evidence is inconclusive.
decisions_risk_reward: In-game decisions and the risk/reward relationship were not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive. A song-selection option and a Warm-up option are visible in the menu, but the consequences of the choice or execution risk cannot be established from these frames.
rewards: Reward, score increase, combo, Fever, or power move was not observed in the screenshots; the available evidence is inconclusive. Items such as combo and Fever appear only in the official card’s claim and were not play-tested.
penalties_failure: Penalty, error, loss, multiplier reduction, or failure was not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive.
outcomes_replay: Win/loss outcome, song end, result screen, or replay was not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive; therefore replay capability and motivation to repeat also cannot be determined from the available evidence.
onboarding: The menu page shows a Warm-up option labeled Guided tutorial stage and a HOW TO PLAY option. The page text says to enter the arrows and press Space on beat 4; this is text/menu-based onboarding, and educational success or stage execution was not observed.
visual_audio_accessibility: The screenshots show a neon 3D scene, colored lights, a logo, and a high-contrast menu. The page text mentions Original music and Dance mocap: AIST++ (CC BY 4.0) and recommends headphones; actual sound was not heard. Subtitle status, volume adjustment, color-blindness support, reduced motion, and other accessibility features were not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive.
technical_clues: The metadata recorded two canvases with dimensions 1280×800; this is a possible technical clue for canvas rendering, not proof of game logic.
The resources recorded 7 scripts, one stylesheet, 32 images, 38 fetches, and one XHR; the code was not scanned and no tuning constant or engine marker was recorded.
An AudioContext warning says that sound must start after a user gesture; this is a possible clue of a browser audio limitation and does not establish music execution.
A fallback to software WebGL warning was recorded; this may affect rendering, but does not establish the cause of the frame change or game behavior.
transferable_principles: Introduce multi-step inputs with short, visible text and keep success feedback separate from loading progress.
An optional tutorial path and a quick-start path in the initial menu can simplify user entry.
For time-based games, direct and recognizable feedback should be visible in the same frame as active execution; a frame change alone is insufficient to prove input acceptance.
Claim the cost and risk of decisions only when their consequences have been recorded in observable execution.
candle_climber_relevance: For Candle Climber, any score or rank should reflect only player skill and execution, not purchases or a wallet, and not an economic advantage.
The general pattern of introducing a tutorial stage and clearly displaying controls can be used for onboarding, but the climbing loop and outcome must be tested separately through actual execution.

Do not copy free brake, horizontal direction change, or a branch path requiring new controls; adding any of these is only a hypothesis requiring independent testing, not a conclusion from this evidence.
Do not generalize this game’s claims about combo, Fever, or competition to Candle Climber mechanics; these items were not observed during active play in this review.
do_not_copy: Do not reproduce this game’s name, character, logo, scene, art, asset, or distinctive text.
Do not copy the official card’s claims about songs, rivals, combo, Fever, or special moves as confirmed mechanics.
Avoid conclusions about input acceptance, win/loss, or the game loop based solely on a change between two frames.
Do not reproduce the sound, brand, mocap, or any asset mentioned on the page as an implementation suggestion for another game.

evidence.claim: The load frame shows only the loading scene and 9%; no active or controllable game element is visible.
The after_start stage text says to enter the arrows and press Space on beat 4; input acceptance is not visible in the frame.
In after_key_burst, the same textual instruction remains and loading progress of 85% is visible; this change does not prove input acceptance.
The after_combined_input frame shows the menu page: PLAY, song selection, WARM-UP, HOW TO PLAY, SETTINGS, and the arrow/Space/Esc instructions.
The late frame still shows the main menu, and neither active gameplay nor a result is observed.
The official card claims that fast arrow chains, beats, competition with three rivals, combo, Fever, power move, and four tracks exist; this claim was not confirmed through gameplay.
The metadata records a visual change but explicitly warns that animation or elapsed time could be its cause, and input acceptance was not established.
AudioContext requires resume after a user gesture, and a software WebGL fallback was recorded; these are possible technical clues.

limitations: Only evidence.json and five current frames of this game were reviewed; no web browsing, rerun, code scan, or hidden-control testing was performed. There is no frame showing active gameplay, a repeatable loop, score, result, or failure. The after_start and after_key_burst stages are still loading pages, while after_combined_input and late are the main menu. The absence of an element in the opening frame does not establish its absence from the game as a whole.
